purpose: The public data stack this library is allowed to build on. Every sourced value and every grounded driver range must trace to one of these. Recording them here makes 'where did this number come from' answerable without reading the manifest that used it.
principle: A model never holds a hardcoded number that isn't real. Where no disclosed point value exists, the cell is a driver whose RANGE is grounded in one of these sources -- most often industry statistics rather than a company-specific disclosure. That is why the industry-statistics source below matters as much as the filings source.

sources.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission -- EDGAR
sources.access: public, no licence restriction on facts
grounds: share counts, capital structure, debt schedules
M&A terms via merger proxies and S-4 filings
sources.environment_note: Direct fetch returns HTTP 403 from this sandbox's egress. Reached instead through a connector, or recorded to tools/data_fabric/out/ from a session that had access.

sources.name: U.S. Department of the Treasury
grounds: risk-free rate for discounting and WACC builds
term structure for fixed-income and rates models

sources.name: FRED -- Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Economic Data
grounds: macro time series (GDP, CPI, unemployment, fed funds)
equity index history for realised volatility and drawdown
sources.cadence: varies by series; most monthly or daily

sources.name: Damodaran Online -- NYU Stern industry datasets
grounds: industry cost of capital and cost of equity
industry operating margins, effective tax rates, reinvestment rates
sources.cadence: annual (January refresh), with some series updated more often
sources.why_it_matters: This is the source that lets a driver range be grounded rather than invented. An entry multiple for a buyout that never happened has no disclosed value -- but the observed distribution of EV/EBITDA multiples for that industry is a real, published statistic, and a range built from it is sourced rather than fabricated.

sources.name: Yahoo Finance
sources.usage_note: Used as a data input for building models, which is what it is published for. This library records facts with attribution and does not republish or redistribute the underlying dataset.

grounding_policy.observed: A disclosed value for the specific subject, from sec_edgar, an issuer disclosure, or a primary market source.
grounding_policy.derived: Arithmetic on observed values, with the derivation stated (e.g. D&A / revenue).
grounding_policy.grounded_driver: A scenario driver whose range comes from a named industry statistic -- typically damodaran, fred, or us_treasury -- rather than from a point disclosure about the subject.
grounding_policy.forbidden: A hardcoded number with no traceable basis. This is the failure mode every other rule here exists to prevent.
